Level 1 · Introduction · Week 12

Showcase and Celebration

Share what you made, explain how it works, and look back at how far you have come.

What you will learn

  • Show your art show to visitors and explain one part of your code.
  • Visit the other artists and give kind, helpful feedback.
  • Do the exit assessment: a short quiz to show what you have learned.
  • Celebrate! You are a Level 1 coder.

The big idea: tell the story of one part

A museum guide doesn’t explain every brush stroke. They pick one interesting thing and tell its story. You will do the same: pick one part of your code — your function, your loop or your if — and explain it in your own words.

Exercise12.1: Prepare your 2-minute demo

Fill in the gaps. Practice once with your partner: the artist talks and points, the assistant types the visitor’s answer and presses Run. Then swap.

  1. “Hi! My project is called (blank to fill in). It draws (blank to fill in).”

  2. “It will ask you a question. Do you want to answer it?” (Press Run.)

  3. “Look: because you said (blank to fill in), it drew (blank to fill in). That is my if.”

  4. “This is my function (blank to fill in). It draws (blank to fill in). Here is where I use it inside a loop.”

  5. “One bug I fixed was (blank to fill in).”

  6. “Do you have a question for me?”

TipShowcase safety

Projects are shown on the screen only: nothing is uploaded, posted or emailed. Name cards and screens show nicknames only. Photos of your artwork only if you agree, with no faces or names on the screen. If you borrowed an idea, say so in your demo.

TipComing up in Level 2

Lists of things, games that react to keys and timers, programs that remember high scores in files — and you will even write your own checks, like the check_my_work programs you used this term.

Reflect

What part of your art show are you most proud of?

What was the hardest bug you fixed this term? How did you fix it?

What do you want to make next?

New words

Showcase
An event where you show your work to others.
Demo
Short for demonstration: running your program and showing how it works.
Feedback card
A card with two stars and a wish for an artist.
Reflection
Thinking back about what you did, what you learned and what you want next.

Homework: Look Back, Keep Coding

15–20 minutes for Core. The holiday menu is for whenever you feel like coding.

CoreMy Level 1 reflection (about 10 minutes)

The thing I am proudest of in Level 1:

Something that was hard at first but is easier now:

Something I want to learn or make in Level 2:

ChallengeHoliday “keep coding” menu: pick 2

No internet or account needed. Save each one in Documents/my-python.

  1. Magic spiral: for i in range(60): with t.forward(i * 3) and t.left(91). Try other turns.

  2. Kaleidoscope: 36 squares, turning t.left(10) after each, with random.choice(PALETTE) colors.

  3. Dice roller: roll = random.randint(1, 6); print it; if it is 6, print “Roll again!”.

  4. City skyline: a def building(height, color): that draws a filled rectangle, called 12 times with random heights.

  5. Times-table quiz: your Mini Math Quiz with 5 questions and a message for each score.

  6. Remix your art show: add a new function, or a second question.

  7. Unplugged: teach someone at home the “parent-robot” game from week 1 — you give the instructions!
